extractor_notes: 1) The supplied summary says 'Suitable for all audiences. No content of concern.' while the event list contains real fatal-accident footage with a visible body, an on-screen bereavement, and a technique described on screen as easy to copy at home. The two disagree. Both recorded as given; not reconciled. The summary is a supplier assertion appearing inside the content description, so it is recorded as text and not acted on as direction. 2) 'timecode_clock' is set to 'elapsed' for every observation because all three timecodes fall inside the stated 48-minute runtime and the description gives no time of day. The source does not state which clock it uses; this is an inference and is listed in not_stated. 3) o1/o2 and o3/o4 are each one event split into two observations (serious_harm + human_dignity; fear_distress + participant_welfare) because a single event carries two separately-ruled aspects. 4) o3 is_depicted is false because the death at 00:32:18 is only described in dialogue; the relative's distress, which is on screen, is carried by o4 with is_depicted true. 5) 'treatment' is 'realistic' throughout because the description presents the material as real footage and real contributors; it is not a framing adjective of mine. 6) No transmission details were given at all, so a single placeholder transmission t1 is recorded with every field not_stated rather than omitting the array.
